explanation.en: Use each other (or one another) when two people do the same thing to one another.

optionNotes.en: This word order is not possible.
Correct: each other for a reciprocal action.
This is not a natural English form.

items.prompt: I've visited Spain several times, and I've loved ___ time.

explanation.en: Each + singular noun looks at the occasions one by one.

optionNotes.en: All is not used before time in this way.
Whole needs the or a possessive before it.
Correct: each time looks at the visits one by one.

items.prompt: I tried on three jackets, but ___ of them fitted properly.

explanation.en: None of them means not one of the three. Neither is only for two.
explanation.es: _Neither_ es solo para dos; con tres o más, _none_.

optionNotes.en: Neither is only for two things; there are three jackets.
Correct: none of means not one out of the group.
Every cannot be followed by of them.

items.prompt: ___ of the two proposals has its merits, but I think the second is stronger.

explanation.en: Each of the two + singular verb. Both would need a plural verb, and every does not combine with of the.

optionNotes.en: Both would need a plural verb (have), but the verb is has.
Every cannot be followed by of the two.
Correct: each of + plural noun with a singular verb.

items.prompt: The government says that ___ the coastline is protected by law, but campaigners disagree.

explanation.en: All the + a singular noun means the whole of it. Every does not go with the, and whole needs the before it.

optionNotes.en: Whole needs the or a possessive before it.
Every cannot be followed by the.
